# JailBee

> JailBee runs isolated, per-branch development environments in Incus system
> containers. Every git branch gets a full container of its own — its own
> services, its own IP, and optionally its own Docker daemon and its own IDE
> and browser on your desktop — so several stacks run in parallel on one Linux
> host without port conflicts, Docker name clashes or shared-database
> collisions. It is also a sandbox for coding agents: the container is the
> boundary, so an agent can run unattended with permission prompts turned off.

JailBee is a Python CLI (`jailbee`, short form `jb`) that wraps the `incus`
command. It is project-agnostic: every repository supplies its own committed
`.jailbee/config.yaml` declaring what its containers need — bind mounts,
devices, egress allowlist, shared caches, and what boots on create. Install
with `uv tool install jailbee` or `pipx install jailbee`.

Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later. Built at GISGRO Oy, which is its origin, not its
scope.

## What makes it different

- **Isolation by boundary, not by allowlist.** Most agent sandboxes enumerate
  which paths, hosts and syscalls are permitted, so every new tool the agent
  reaches for is a policy change. JailBee moves the boundary instead: the
  container is the fence, and what happens inside it is unconstrained.
- **A system container, not an application container.** It runs its own init,
  its own systemd services, and — when the repo enables the Docker stack — its
  own Docker daemon (nested, `security.nesting`), so the repo's existing
  `docker-compose.yml` runs unmodified.
- **Per-container egress allowlist** enforced by a kernel-level ACL, written
  as hostnames and ports (`api.example.com:443`) rather than IP ranges, and
  covering any protocol — `ssh`, `git+ssh` and database clients included, not
  just HTTP. `*.example.com` wildcards are accepted too; they pass through an
  egress proxy, so they cover HTTP(S) clients that honour `HTTPS_PROXY`.
  `github.com` is deliberately absent from the strict default so an
  unattended agent cannot surprise-push.
- **The container is a git remote.** `jailbee git push/pull/fetch/checkout/diff`
  move commits between host and container without a round trip through GitHub,
  and `jailbee git merge` merges one container's branch into another's.
  Submodules travel with the superproject. `jailbee pr` opens or updates the
  GitHub PR from a container's branch, with the title and body written by the
  in-container Claude — to the project's own standard when the repo states one
  in `claude.pr_prompt`.
- **Host services reach in, opt-in.** A declared forward
  (`host_ports: [{ name: adb, port: 5037 }]`) makes a host service reachable on
  every container's own localhost — an adb server with a phone attached, a
  database — and `jailbee port` adds or removes one ad hoc, in either
  direction. Forwards are Incus proxy devices, so they bypass the egress ACL by
  construction; `jailbee net status` lists the open ones next to the allowlist.
- **One dashboard across every repo.** A live, mouse-enabled TUI
  (`jailbee dashboard`, also what bare `jailbee` opens) or Qt GUI
  (`jailbee gui`) lists every container on the host and acts on it — shell,
  tmux, IDE, create or update the PR, update from base, read the diff, follow a
  background job's log — each offered only when it would do something.
- **GUI passthrough.** A JetBrains IDE and Chrome run *inside* the container
  and render on the host's Wayland session, reaching the container's own
  `localhost:3000`. Five containers can each serve port 3000 with nothing to
  forward and no collisions.
- **Snapshots** before an agent run, restore after.

## What people run in it

- A mobile app with a shared Android/iOS core, split across eight containers,
  each with its own Android emulator on the host's `/dev/kvm`, with the
  dashboard showing which agent is waiting.
- A backlog of small improvements: one container and one agent per idea,
  merged back to main through the git bridge.
- A Compose stack per branch: its own Docker daemon, Compose project, database
  and localhost.
- Reviewing a pull request in a container of its own (`jailbee new --pr N`)
  without disturbing the developer's branch.
- An agent working without permission prompts behind a strict egress
  allowlist, with PRs and issues staged in an outbox for a human to publish.
- A supervised admin task with time-boxed credentials: an optional mount and
  loose network mode that both revert on a timer.

## When not to use it

- **Not on macOS or Windows.** JailBee itself runs on Linux only. A Mac or a
  Windows machine can use one as a client, over the SSH service and the
  shared RDP display; running it in a Linux VM on a Mac is experimental.
- **Not if you need a hypervisor boundary.** A system container shares the
  host kernel, so a kernel bug is an escape path. Docker Sandboxes (`docker
  sbx`) gives a microVM with its own kernel and is the stronger boundary.
- **Not if your stack is one process and one database.** `git worktree` plus
  `docker compose -p` is free and already installed.
- **Not free to adopt.** Host setup (Incus, UID delegation, firewall, kernel
  keyring limits) is a one-time afternoon, and the golden image takes 10–15
  minutes to build once per repo stack.
- **No editor set up for you beyond JetBrains.** `jailbee ide` accepts the
  JetBrains launcher names and there is no Dev Containers integration. VS Code
  is not ruled out — the GUI passthrough is generic, so installing it into the
  golden image and launching it from a shell works — but nothing ships to wire
  it up.

## Documentation

- [FAQ](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/faq/): short answers to the common questions, indexed into the rest of the documentation
- [Installation](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/installation/): one-time host setup — Incus, UID delegation, installing the CLI
- [Storage: use btrfs](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/storage/): why a copy-on-write btrfs pool beats the default dir pool, and how to set one up
- [Getting started](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/getting-started/): concepts, configuring a repo, building the image, a typical day
- [Commands](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/commands/): full command and flag reference
- [Git bridge](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/git-bridge/): host↔container git bridge, stacked PRs, PR review
- [Configuration reference](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/config/): every `.jailbee/config.yaml` and `global.yaml` key
- [Generic agent support](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/agents/): the `agents:` config key, the six shipped presets (Claude Code plus five best-effort templates), and how to add one of your own
- [Security and limitations](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/security/): isolation model and known limits, including what running an agent without prompts does and does not cover
- [Who JailBee is for](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/comparison/): how it compares to Dev Containers, BranchBox, nono, Docker Sandboxes and Microsoft MXC, when not to use it, and what it costs — every caveat, and the sources each claim was checked against
- [Architecture](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/architecture/): how the pieces fit together

## Optional

- [Setting up JailBee in your own project](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/project-config/): adapting it to your own repo and stack
- [Using JailBee from a Mac](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/macos/): a Linux host with the Mac as client, or an experimental Linux VM on the Mac
- [Troubleshooting](https://jailbee.gisgro.io/docs/troubleshooting/): common failures by symptom
- [Source repository](https://github.com/VRTFinland/jailbee)
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/jailbee/)
